item.title: Re: Tectonic Watchers
item.content:encoded:
That sounds really interesting and dynamic. So maybe you'll want to expand on why they cause these earthquakes in some way whether that be a flat out answer, a mostly mysterious hint, or what have you. Given that the foundation commonly works to avoid disasters, they likely wouldn't attempt an all-out war without the certain leverage or answers of some other SCPs at the foundation's disposal. I could absolutely see them preparing repair/response teams to either stop/lessen the quakes and/or repair the damages & people and predictions could actually fit really well with that. The most interesting and probably difficult way would be for the Foundation to establish some form of agreement of peace. Remember: Secure, Contain, Protect. Think about what's going into the procedures portion.

item.title: Ovda Regio - Aphrodite
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article/GoI

Genre (Optional): Galactic, Mystery

Page Layout (Optional): ACS header, basic layout, and exploration logs.

Elevator Pitch: Venus, a dead toxic planet believed to have no life on it, just sent signals to the SCP foundation, and no one knows who or why they did it, but they'll find out one way or another.

Central Narrative: (SCP) The SCP is currently classified as a signal, mainly because the origin is not yet located, and no one knows where it's precise location is, besides the fact it's located in the Ovda Regio, a massive landform (5280 km) located in the Aphrodite landmass. No one knows if it's a lost tribe, a massive monster, or a distress signal. Signals usually come in an unknown translation of code, and impossible to decipher.

(GoI) The team designated to the Ovda Regio is the ORET (Ovda Regio Exploration Team). They are responsible for scanning the OR in search of the origin of the signal, hoping they don't die from the harsh elements. Because of the toxic environment, limited time on the ground, and the amount of knowledge about the lands, the origin will take a very long time to locate, and has a possibility of not being found at all.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The most interesting part will 100% be the exploration logs, as there are an abundance of them, and they all are full of interesting content.

Additional Notes: If you want to know what the Ovda Regio is, here's a link. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovda_Regio

item.title: Re: Tectonic Watchers
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for responding!

I intend for the MTF unit to originally only stay there to gain more Intel, however slowly come to learn that it's actually an entire race of people which are seemingly god-like. The reason they took him is because he's the first non-light entity to attempt to interact with them in all of history. Of course they know about humans, but not much as they only seem to watch earthquakes or other catastrophic events such as Volcanoes and the like.
He'd slowly figure out most of the information due to inference and suggestion from the entities.
While I haven't directly decided on this 100%, I've been considering the fact that these SCPs are actually revealed to manually move tectonic plates to cause earthquakes, which would be extremely dangerous if they're capable of doing that.
I was considering that due to the nature of the SCPs extreme difficulty to contain and high danger, the SCP Foundation could possibly attempt to even attack the entities whilst they're appearing during an earthquake to neutralize the threat of extreme magnitude seismic activity - (due to specific patterns of locations in which they appear they could possibly predict the location of the next light). That may give the MTF a choice between choosing The Foundation or SCPs. I'd have to decide which they choose from there.
This war could then tie in with the MTF which you mentioned attempting to neutralize the entities seemingly inside of an entire war between these light beings & The Foundation. I'd have to choose how that ends, however. If they're capable of just shifting tectonic plates it could end in a possible XK-Class Scenario, ending the entire world, however I don't know if my first SCP would be allowed to go that far. I'll have to think about the escalation of it a bit more.

Reply to below, as I don't want to further the thread:

You saying that gave me another possible idea that the MTF is actually a "spokesperson" for the light people, and he advocates for the peace between them and delivers messages. I'll continue to think about it as much as I can, as it'd make sense the SCP Foundation wouldn't want to engage war.

item.title: Re: Tectonic Watchers
item.content:encoded:
In the tale itself, you should probably develop in the writing who the protagonist holds allegiance to as the events unfold. Does he hold sympathy towards them, is he still set on getting them into containment, or is he just waiting it out to get away? Why are the lights telling him all this information?
When it comes to the SCP: What is the danger or interesting aspects of these lights themselves? Is this location the lights take him to also a factor in the SCP? The SCP log would benefit if it contains the Foundation's management of the damages if at all. If the foundation is entirely unable to contain, influence, or mitigate the SCP's exposure to the outside world, it just feels sort of useless to read as part of the SCP foundation unless it's tied into other portions of the foundation. I could see potential tie-ins with SCP-1000, MTF Ghost busters, MTF Mole Rats, MTF City Slickers, and MTF White Rabbits if you're comfortable with them. Make sure to include how they are managed by the foundation to the best or their ability.

item.title: Re: A Plushie Friend
item.content:encoded:
Hello!

SCP-#### would be brought home by the field agent, who, when, in tears, hugged the object, would hear a voice calming him down.

Why would the Foundation let him take it home? They never let people keep anomalies.

He would later survive a stray bullet with no damage at all while he slept, hugging the plushie. After that, the field agent would bring the object to the foundation site immediately.

Where does the stray bullet come from.

against some Groups of Interest, who would want to have SCP-#### so they could become invincible.

I don't think you need to include any GOIs, what you have so far looks good enough.

SCP-#### would be discovered by a field agent accidentally, when a little boy hugging the object was run over by a truck and suffered no damage at all. He (the field agent) would keep an eye on the boy for some months, who seemed to have no anomalous properties.

Sounds like a fun idea, try to hide the fact that the plushie is the anomaly at first then reveal it later on, you might need to include multiple iterations of the SCP.

Honestly, I'm liking this. I'm a huge fan of friendly SCPs and this seems to be a really good idea to include some really emotional bits if you write it well.

I'm gonna Greenlight this. There is room for expansion, but it still feels like a cool idea. I like how simple it is, I see a lot of new writers try to use overly complicated ideas before their ready so this looks like a really good place to start for a first time author.

Good luck!

Also, remember you do not need a second Greenlight in order to ask for help on the #thecritters channel.

Hello, and welcome ObtuseGryphon! Trust me, you are not alone in taking your time to write your own SCP, as many of us have waited a long time before thinking about writing our own. It's all about improvement here too, everyone is out to help make your idea the best it can be. And, no matter what the part you struggle on is there is someone that specializes in that department to help you out. You'll do just fine around here. Make sure to take your time and get acquainted with how everything here works, and make sure to check out IRC chat too!

For my recommendation, you should check out SCP-5109

- Hide Resources

Remember that there is no rush, and you should take time familiarizing yourself with how Series 6 articles are formatted. We are a rather unique bunch so I'm sure just reading and being a part of the community will be rather fun for you!

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.


Best of luck!

item.title: Re: How many times should I ask for a critique?
item.content:encoded:
If they leave a placeholder and a time (Such as "Will crit within 24 hours") you can PM them after the time is up to remind them. If they don't respond, don't spam them with requests. If they've critiqued your idea and you've edited it, you can PM them again to see if they'll take another look. If someone tells you no or that they're busy, stop asking them since they're probably busy or just don't want to review it. Honestly, if you act respectfully towards the people doing you a favor, they'll have no issue critiquing you further, assuming time/life/whatever allows.

I suggest PMing more people (that you think, based on the butt squad roster, will be a good fit for critting) and stopping by our Crit Chat (#thecritters, the guide I linked there will teach you everything.) There are a lot more reviewers than just the ones on the butterfly squad roster that will help out there.

I hope this helped!

How many times is it socially acceptable to ask a reviewer to critique your idea via Wikidot PM? I'm new to writing and I've gotten a couple of critiques from people in the Butterfly Squad on my idea.

I understand that most reviewers are busy reviewing and have real life commitments. Would it be annoying for me to ask them to review my idea again after I revised it multiple times? Per the required reading forum guidelines, please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Put yes or no. **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** [How will you will structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? Rather than posting a new comment, edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment.

Remember that the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

item.title: Re: Mandala-Manifested Meadow of Majestic, Melancholic Madness
item.content:encoded:
+ Crit lives within
– hide block

Coherence:

Assuming you meant thematic coherence (due to the Understandability section), this article is a bit all over the place. The nuns, the worms, the mass hysteria, etc., none of it feels like it's properly fit together. Moreover, the Mandala's usage feels largely superficial, especially considering that it felt like a Hindu concept was being forced into a largely Christian framework.

Consistency

Everything from the tulpa onward feels as if it's missing context. The stakes necessary for it to work simply aren't there for much of the piece, and it leads to what feels like a slog through events that don't carry any emotional weight.

Dialogue

Dialogue was alright. Only thing of note was that I found it odd:

Operator: Indeed. The phone says that this fluid's effects include but are not limited to:
1.) Loss of inhibitions.
2.) Steady increase in psychosis-type symptoms.
3.) Dizziness.

Having a character suddenly speak in list form feels off.

Clinical tone

It was fine.

Pacing

The pacing is incredibly off. By the IV portion, the piece read like it was near the end, despite being only 1/3rd the way through. It made the chase scene a major slog. Then the dream ends, and it cuts to the second offset, which feels almost entirely disconnected from the events I read in the log. It's for this reason among others that I recommend removing the second offset.

Additionally, how the "FOOTAGE LOST"s break up sections is very disorientating. It leaves a lot of the earlier sections feeling cut off from one another, without a sense of continuity.

Plot

It didn't seem very good.

As noted above, the piece fails to establish the emotional stakes. I don't know who Hero is; I don't know who the tulpa is. Because I as the reader have no real understanding of these characters, I'm not able to care about everything happening to them. The end result is that the plot feels like a slog through a list of things occurring to characters I neither know or care for.

Additionally, none of the plot feels like it's thematically connected to the anomaly at hand. This is a piece about someone attempting to rescue their tulpa from the dreamscape for a good chunk; however, the overarching "eldritch sponge" aspect barely comes up, and it's only really explored in what amounts to a (figurative) footnote in the final offset. This is especially bad as I heavily recommend you remove it for pacing, among other things.

Understandability

I could understand what was happening perfectly fine, up until the final offset. I don't have any advice on how to fix said offset's understandability, as again, I heavily recommend you remove it.

Is the second list-page even necessary, or can I just remove it and shove the plot reveal into the main page via a collapsible?

100% remove it. It feels overly expository, and the note at the end is unnecessary.

Overall

This piece needs extensive restructuring if it wants to work. The thematics don't feel consistent, the piece feels like it's ending a third of the way through, and the characters don't make enough of an impression to justify the plot of the log.

item.title: Re: A train experience based on guilts
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Zyffin. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So my first question was how exactly does the scp / anomaly work. It’s not explained clearly in your Elevator Pitch. How exactly does the train “exploit the guilts of the beings that enter”?

Furthermore, your Central Narrative is lacking in context – you suddenly mention “human experiments” and “future SCPs” but I don’t understand who is doing what. This section should detail a specific story involving your scp: it could be that of a test subject who encounters the scp. It could be from the perspective of a researcher who is conducting the experiments. Regardless, you need to breakdown what actually happens in the story from beginning to end, and the significance of these events. Right now, you’re merely describing the scp in the further detail – this isn’t a narrative.

Regarding your Hook, I’m afraid this section raises more questions than answers because each statement is vague and doesn’t tell me anything new about the actual anomaly.

Lastly, I’m a little worried your language ability at the moment in order to clearly and succinctly explain the concept. There are frequent grammatical errors in tenses and sentence structure that impair the overall clarity of the concept – I’d recommend during a final check before you post stuff in the future or use an online platform like Grammarly to help look for errors.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I may take another look. All the best!

item.title: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
Okay so I see you've revised the ending based on Grigori's feedback, which I agree with wholeheartedly. But right now, the revised ending is left a little open and unsatisfying.

I know your intention was to leave the answers to those questions unanswered (particularly because they can't be answered easily in the first place), but I think you should still consider something that happens to Sir Reginald that brings his story to a close.

Consider two possible options to end the article:
(1) Sir Reginald takes his own life. Yes, we'd usually discourage this, but if you can justify his actions / sadness / reasons for doing so, it's an entirely plausible ending. I like that interaction between 1 and 2 - your last "shot" or entry, so to speak, could be to show the TV-Reginald smiling, back in his own reality. Even though he killed himself in the real world, he's finally found his own happiness back in the television show.

(2) Sir Reginald finds a NEW purpose in the real world. Maybe he helps the Foundation contain other fictional characters that come to life? Maybe he becomes a consultation on his own television show. Readers do want some element of closure, but which ending you choose will depend on the message you wish to convey to the audience.

Does he have a soul? Is he human? Does he have a purpose? If he can exists in two worlds, how does he know that his current level of existence is real? Is he real?

I've tried to align the possible endings above to your guiding central questions. But it's really your choice at the end of the day. What you have right now don't seem to tackle those themes as much as I'd like.

item.title: Re: Image-Shifting Painting
item.content:encoded:
Hello LeavesOfAutumn! let's take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: The SCP itself is an oil painting titled 'Divide and Conquer' that manifests its anomalous property when observed by one person and one person only. When observed by more, the painting will simply show a painting of Liberty Hall in Philadelphia. When observed by only one person, the image depicted in the painting will change in some way to be related to the person observing.

Personally, this reminds me of SCP-1074, except the painting just shows peoples future misfortunes, rather than showing them something indescribable. Along with this, there doesn't seem to be any particular reason the painting shows the liberty hall of Philadelphia? or any reason why the painting my have been created?- was it to annoy the Foundation? scare people? was it made by AWCY?

The narrative:

Central Narrative: The painting, when observed by only one person, will show events that will happen to or near to that person in the near future. The SCP is discovered after causing mass panic at an art exhibit. The painting predicts deaths, robbery, loss of homes, etc. All these events happen to the people, so the Foundation takes it in for research. When observed by the D-Class, the painting shows minor containment breaches and injury to the researchers assigned to it, all of which come to pass. One day, it shows the complete destruction of the site where it is located. The researchers swiftly alert the site director, and all personnel are about to evacuate before the painting shifts to say 'wowwee, u trolld ursefl!' and changes to a blank white canvas that does not change no matter how many people look at it.

Overall this feels flat to me, as the primary focus seems to be on the painting and its effects, rather than any characters or major conflicts. As it stands, it just feels like D-class are being thrown in there to further showcase what it does. The narrative doesn't really build up (or even really hint) to the painting suddenly deciding it was going to play a joke, nor the narrative really explain why it just turns to white after this event.

Currently, Theres not much of a conflict or rising tension shown here, the narrative as a whole just sort of feels like a random object trolling the Foundation with no context. I think this work better if there was a reason for the painting doing this, as it would allow the narrative to focus on more than just "Foundation finds and tests the skip".- giving it a clearer purpose, may also allow this to seperate itself from SCP-1074, as both are built on fairly similar premises.

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques/perspectives in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

RED

  • Based off Octopuses(Still on fence on how big)
  • Safe

Central Narrative:
The foundation finds this SCP(either from aquarium/research center/ appears on their doorstep) and contains it. Only to start finding childish pranks being pulled around the site with an unknown snicker following. Water buckets over doorways, Gum under door handles, childish sticky notes, kick me signs on researcher's back. When they review tapes they note the SCP breaks containment and then returns back after completing the pranks. They put it in more secure containment. Only to see no matter what measures they put in place, it escapes. It doesn't escape via teleporting, phasing or anything like that. It will social engineer, pick locks, trick, squeeze through tiny gaps..ect..ect.

A researcher takes notice they begin experimenting on it. Then they start to use it to test containment chambers and reward it. They will at times use it to test security at other sites. Since it is clear, this SCP could have left the site at anytime it chose to. The SCP becomes attached to a particular researcher and will often escape to be near them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It is a friendly SCP that benefits the foundation with a lighthearted/fun story.

item.title: SCP-XXXX "Unlucky Bill"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): General SCP Article layout. After the description comes an interview with the SCP, followed by a listing of the items Bill has "lost" and then a few tests that the Foundation ran to determine the origin and parameters of bills condition.

Elevator Pitch: The various items SCP-XXXX "loses" aren't just lost like you and me lose a key. When Bill "loses" an item, it is permanently removed from our reality and can't be found/traced.

Central Narrative: Bill was first found by the Foundation when his sister asked him to take care of her infant daughter for 5 minutes. Bill laid her down on some soft spot to close curtains because it was thundering outside. When he got distracted, he forgot for a short moment where he placed the infant, and so when he turned around, the baby was gone and never found again. Bill was placed under arrest after his sister's husband called the police and when they were clueless as to what he could have done with the infant, the foundation got involved.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP-XXXX's condition which leaves the researchers of the foundation puzzling and the tests that are run while trying to determine its parameters.
